decision.explanation: The matrix maps (x,y) to (-x,y), reversing the x-coordinate while preserving the y-coordinate. This is reflection across the y-axis.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: What linear transformation $T$ is represented by the matrix $T=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]?$
after.worked_solution:
Consider the standard basis ${i,j}$ of the Euclidean plane ${R}^{2}$ and the unit square spanned by the vectors, as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14098643/assets/9e322e6ed1ddb8f1d094633e931cd179b7eb9d6f47acd7c7d0809f113df91b22.png)

Now, we compute the images of ${i,j}$ under $T$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{i}^{′} & =T(i)=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=-i \\ {j}^{′} & =T(j)=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=j\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we obtain the following image:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14098643/assets/86adc8f8f32a097b0506adbe15da962e34aad904bf603714bac5cd27712095c8.png)

Therefore, the matrix represents a reflection across the $y$-axis.

i′=T(i)=[−1001][10]=[−10]=−ij′=T(j)=[−1001][01]=[01]=j

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: A linear transformation $T$ represents a dilation.  Given that $v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]$ and $T(v)=[\begin{aligned}48 \\ -32\end{aligned}],$ what is the standard matrix of $T?$
after.worked_solution:
We can write $T(v)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(v) & =[\begin{aligned}48 \\ -32\end{aligned}] \\  & =16\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =16v\end{aligned}
$$

So we have $T(v)=16v,$ and so the linear transformation $T$ is a dilation with scale factor $k=16.$

The matrix that represents a dilation of scale factor $k$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}k & 0 \\ 0 & k\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the standard matrix of $T$ is

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}16 & 0 \\ 0 & 16\end{aligned}].
$$

after.problem:
A  linear transformation $T$ represents a dilation. Given that $v=[\begin{aligned}-10 \\ 5\end{aligned}]$ and $T(v)=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 2\end{aligned}],$ what is the standard matrix $T$ of $T?$

| $T=\,\,$ |  | {{field-1}} | {{field-2}} |  |

after.worked_solution:
We can write $T(v)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(v) & =[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{2}{5}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-10 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{2}{5}v\end{aligned}
$$

So we have $T(v)=\frac{2}{5}v,$ and so the linear transformation $T$ is a dilation with scale factor $k=\frac{2}{5}.$

The matrix that represents a dilation of scale factor $k$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}k & 0 \\ 0 & k\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the standard matrix of $T$ is

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{5} & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{2}{5}\end{aligned}].
$$
